'''Olivia Lum Ooi Lin''' is a Singaporean businesswoman. She is the founder, group chief executive officer, and former president of the [[Singapore]]-based [[Hyflux|Hyflux Group]].<ref name="Smith">{{Cite magazine |last=Lloyd-Smith |first=David |date=5 April 2004 |title=The Moisture Merchant: Dealing in Liquid Assets |url=https://content.time.com/time/specials/packages/printout/0,29239,1995235_1995382_1995530,00.html?iid=sr-link2 |access-date=15 January 2008 |magazine=[[Time Magazine]]}}</ref><ref name="Self">{{Cite news |last=Lum |first=Olivia |date=4 June 2007 |title=Toilet was just a squat pan; Group CEO and president of Hyflux Olivia Lum recounts a childhood of extreme poverty |url=http://newpaper.asia1.com.sg/printfriendly/0,4139,132153,00.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071223005230/http://newpaper.asia1.com.sg/printfriendly/0,4139,132153,00.html |archive-date=23 December 2007 |access-date=15 January 2008 |work=The Electric New Paper |publisher=Singapore }}</ref><ref name="Xinhua">{{citation |last=Zhang |first=Lihong |title=新加坡"水之女皇"林爱莲 幽默随和的美丽女人/Singapore's 'Queen of Water' Olivia Lum - a humorous, amiable beauty |date=6 October 2005 |periodical=Xinhua News |url=http://news.xinhuanet.com/world/2005-10/06/content_3587618.htm |access-date=15 January 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071204164449/http://news.xinhuanet.com/world/2005-10/06/content_3587618.htm |archive-date=4 December 2007 |url-status=dead |language=zh}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=SUSTAINABLE SOLUTIONS THAT TRANSFORM LIVES |url=https://www.hyflux.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/07/HyfluxFactSheet_Jun-2016.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170716150020/https://www.hyflux.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/07/HyfluxFactSheet_Jun-2016.pdf |archive-date=16 July 2017 |access-date=18 March 2022}}</ref>

==Early life==
Lum was adopted at birth, and never knew her biological parents; she was brought up by a woman she called her "grandmother". When Lum was only three, her grandmother gambled away her savings; they lost the house in which they were living, and moved to a shack without running water.<ref name="Smith" /> She came to Singapore at the age of 15 and enrolled at the [[Tiong Bahru Secondary School]],<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Zhuo |first=Tee |date=16 February 2019 |title=Hyflux in hot water: 6 things about embattled CEO Olivia Lum |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/business/hyflux-in-hot-water-6-things-about-embattled-ceo-olivia-lum |access-date=20 August 2025 |work=[[The Straits Times]] |language=en |issn=0585-3923}}</ref> where she supported herself through tutoring and sales jobs. She went on to study at [[Hwa Chong Junior College]]<ref name=":0" /> and graduated in 1986 with an Honours degree in chemistry from the [[Faculty of Science, National University of Singapore|Faculty of Science]] of the [[National University of Singapore]].<ref name=":0" />

==Career==
Lum started corporate life as a chemist with [[GlaxoSmithKline|Glaxo Pharmaceutical]]. After working for three years at Glaxo, she left in 1989 at the age of 28 to start up Hydrochem,<ref>{{Cite news |title=Former HR manager of Hyflux subsidiary Hydrochem charged with corruption |url=https://www.channelnewsasia.com/business/hyflux-subsidiary-hydrochem-corruption-former-hr-manager-646236 |access-date=27 January 2023 |work=[[CNA (TV network)|Channel NewsAsia]] |language=en}}</ref> the precursor to [[Hyflux]], with just [[Singapore dollar|SG$]]20,000 of capital, which she raised by selling her condominium and car.<ref name="Self" /> She hired three employees at the start; Lum herself rode around on a motorcycle selling her company's water filters and treatment chemicals.<ref name="Xinhua" /> By January 2001, Hyflux had become the first water treatment company to be listed on [[SESDAQ]], and was upgraded to the [[Singapore Exchange]]'s Mainboard in April 2003.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Pek |first=Tiong Gee |date=2 September 2021 |title=Hyflux: Down the slippery slope |url=https://www.theedgesingapore.com/issues/1000th-issue/hyflux-down-slippery-slope |work=[[The Edge (Malaysia)|The Edge]]}}</ref>

In 2002, Lim won the Her World Woman award of the Year for her contributions to Singaporean water.<ref>{{Cite web |date=17 August 2002 |title=Her World Woman of the Year 2002: Olivia Lum |url=https://www.herworld.com/pov/people/olivia-lum-woman-of-the-year-2002 |access-date=10 November 2024 |website=Her World Singapore |language=en-SG}}</ref> She was also a [[Nominated Member of Parliament]] for a single term from 2002 to 2004.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Hyflux trial as it happened: Prosecutors lay out case against founder Olivia Lum, ex-CFO and directors |url=https://www.channelnewsasia.com/singapore/olivia-lum-trial-hyflux-tuaspring-live-5287286 |access-date=21 January 2026 |website=[[CNA (TV network)|CNA]] |language=en}}</ref>

By 2005, she had a net worth of over US$240 million, which earned her a place as the only woman on ''[[Forbes]]''<nowiki/>' "Southeast Asia Rich List".

Lum holds several positions in public service. She is a board member of [[Statutory boards of the Singapore Government|SPRING Singapore]], the National University Singapore Council, and the Singapore Exchange, as well as the president of the [[Singapore Water Association]]. She is also a member of the [[UNESCAP]] Business Advisory Council and the [[Singapore Green Plan 2012]] coordinating committee.<ref>{{cite web |title=DSA 2005 LUM Ooi Lin Olivia |url=http://science.nus.edu.sg/alumni/science-alumni-awards/distinguished-science-alumni/30-alumni-and-careers/alumni/453-dsa-2005-lum-ooi-lin-olivia |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170316163107/http://www.science.nus.edu.sg/alumni/science-alumni-awards/distinguished-science-alumni/30-alumni-and-careers/alumni/453-dsa-2005-lum-ooi-lin-olivia |archive-date=16 March 2017 |website=science.nus.edu.sg}}</ref> Lum was a [[Nominated Member of Parliament]] in the [[Parliament of Singapore]] from 2 July 2002 to 1 January 2005.<ref name="Bloomberg profile">{{Cite web |title=Lum Ooi Lin "Olivia" |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/profile/person/3875194 |website=[[Bloomberg News]]}}</ref> In 2003, she was awarded the International Management Action Award, followed by the Global Female Invent and Innovate Award the following year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Subramaniam |first=Shivaranjani |date=22 June 2009 |title=Olivia Lum |url=https://www.nlb.gov.sg/main/article-detail?cmsuuid=296713a7-6dfd-40b6-89bb-7a4b2fa183ae |access-date=20 August 2025 |publisher=[[National Library Board]]}}</ref>

On 3 October 2008, Lum resigned her position as independent non-executive director of the [[Singapore Exchange]] and relinquished her position on the audit, regulatory conflicts and remuneration committees of the Exchange, according to the Exchange's filing. She stated this was due to her heavy work commitments in line with Hyflux's rapid expansion, and that her resignation would enable her to focus more time and resources on Hyflux's growth.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Lee |first=Jamie |date=9 September 2008 |title=Hyflux chief to leave SGX board |work=[[The Business Times (Singapore)|The Business Times]] |location=Singapore}}</ref>

In 2011, Lum was named [[Ernst & Young Entrepreneur of the Year Award#21st century recipients|Ernst & Young World Entrepreneur Of The Year]] and was the first woman to win the award.<ref>{{Cite web |date=6 June 2011 |title=Olivia Lum is first woman to win Ernst & Young World Entrepreneur Of The Year Award |url=https://sbr.com.sg/markets-investing/more-news/olivia-lum-first-woman-win-ernst-young-world-entrepreneur-year-award |access-date=30 March 2023 |website=Singapore Business Review |language=en}}</ref>

In 2013, Lum was appointed to the board at [[International Enterprise Singapore]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=30 April 2013 |title=Hyflux's Olivia Lum appointed to IE Singapore board |url=http://www.asiaone.com/business/hyfluxs-olivia-lum-appointed-ie-singapore-board |work=[[Asiaone]]}}</ref>

In 2014 Lum was appointed the board of [[ST Engineering|Singapore Technologies Engineering]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=CHIA |first=YAN MIN |date=22 March 2018 |title=Hyflux's Olivia Lum to retire from ST Engineering board due to business commitments |url=https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/companies-markets/hyfluxs-olivia-lum-to-retire-from-st-engineering-board-due-to-business-commitments}}</ref> She was also inducted into the [[Singapore Women's Hall of Fame]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Olivia Lum |url=https://www.swhf.sg/profiles/olivia-lum/ |access-date=21 January 2026 |website=Singapore Women's Hall of Fame |language=en-GB}}</ref>

In 2016, Lum became a laureate of the [[Asian Scientist 100]] by the ''[[Asian Scientist]]''.<ref>{{cite web |author=<!--Not stated--> |title=The Asian Scientist 100 |url=https://www.asianscientist.com/as100/ |access-date=13 March 2025 |publisher=[[Asian Scientist]]}}</ref>

In 2018, Lum resigned from the board of ST Engineering (previously known as Singapore Technologies Engineering) citing business commitments as her reason for resignation.<ref name=":1" />

In May 2018, Hyflux applied to the Singapore High Court for a 30-day protection against creditor claims to allow the company time to reorganize its liabilities.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Tan |first1=Hwee Hwee |date=23 May 2018 |title=Hyflux seeks court protection to reorganise debt pile |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/business/companies-markets/hyflux-seeks-court-protection-to-reorganise-debt-pile |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221127073425/http://www.straitstimes.com/business/companies-markets/hyflux-seeks-court-protection-to-reorganise-debt-pile |archive-date=27 November 2022 |newspaper=[[The Straits Times]] |access-date=1 August 2018 }}</ref> Following this voluntary filing, Lum announced a series of three townhall meetings with the company's 50,000 plus retail shareholders.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Tang |first=See Kit |date=21 June 2018 |title=Hyflux founder-CEO Olivia Lum to attend townhall meetings with shareholders next month - Channel NewsAsia |url=https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/business/hyflux-founder-ceo-olivia-lum-to-attend-townhall-meetings-with-10456224 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180801155208/https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/business/hyflux-founder-ceo-olivia-lum-to-attend-townhall-meetings-with-10456224 |archive-date=1 August 2018 |access-date=1 August 2018}}</ref> In July, Lum announced that efforts would be made to “ensure that the company stays viable.” Lum also noted that Hyflux had total debt of $1.17 billion.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Leong |first=Grace |date=19 July 2018 |title=CEO Olivia Lum says Hyflux has total debt of $2.95b and is in talks with 8 bidders for Tuaspring plant |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/business/ceo-olivia-lum-says-hyflux-has-total-debt-of-295-billion-and-is-in-talks-with-8-bidders-for |newspaper=[[The Straits Times]]}}</ref>

In December 2022, it was reported that Hyflux was claiming damages exceeding S$690.6 million from Lum in a civil lawsuit alleging [[negligence]] and [[Fiduciary#Breaches of duty and remedies|breach of fiduciary duty]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Tay |first=Peck Gek |date=22 December 2022 |title=Hyflux sues Olivia Lum for more than S$690 million over alleged negligence, fiduciary duty breach |url=https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/companies-markets/capital-markets-currencies/hyflux-sues-olivia-lum-more-s690-million-over-alleged |newspaper=[[The Business Times (Singapore)|The Business Times]]}}</ref>

==Criminal Charges==
On 17 November 2022, Lum, ex-CFO Cho Wee Peng and four other former board members were charged with violations of Singapore's Securities and Futures Act.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Leong |first=Grace |date=17 November 2022 |title=Ex-Hyflux CEO Olivia Lum, ex-CFO and four others charged with violations of Securities and Futures Act |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/business/ex-hyflux-ceo-olivia-lum-ex-cfo-and-four-others-charged-for-violations-of-securities-and-futures-act |access-date=4 May 2023 |work=[[The Straits Times]]}}</ref> On 5 May 2023, Singapore's State Court added three additional charges against Lum, citing violations of the Companies Act related to an allegation that she failed to exercise diligence in the discharge of her duties as a director. Lum faces a potential jail term of up to two years, a maximum fine of S$150,000, or both.<ref name="charges">{{Cite news |last=Leong |first=Grace |date=5 May 2023 |title=Hyflux founder Olivia Lum faces 3 more charges, independent director Lee Joo Hai arrested and charged |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/business/hyflux-founder-olivia-lum-faces-3-more-charges-independent-director-lee-joo-hai-arrested-and-charged#:~:text=Lum%20was%20first%20charged%20in,the%20Securities%20and%20Futures%20Act. |access-date=4 May 2023 |work=[[The Straits Times]]}}</ref>
